history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - KEEP-OR-DROP DECISION NEEDED. Rasiya Ki Tekri is a historic hillock monument and public viewpoint in Tonk city (Astal Road area), not a religious structure. Local history says a Kayastha lover sat here singing love songs (rasiya), giving the tekri (hillock) its name; it was renovated/modernised in 1859 by Shri Ambaji Maharaj, a scholar and composer of love songs appointed governor of the place by Raja Holkar. Today it is listed as a tourist attraction (viewpoint/park) open round the clock. No deity, worship or festival is attached to it.

name: Rasiya Ki Tekri
town_description: Rasiya Ki Tekri sits on a small hillock on Astal Road in Tonk city, about 2.5 km from the city centre, offering a panoramic view of the town. It is a popular local picnic and sunset viewpoint rather than a place of worship.
tradition: None - historic civic monument/viewpoint, not a religious site
